text: This note says $100 trillion. On its first day, it was worth about $30. How do you get
there? In November 2008, prices in Zimbabwe were rising about 98% a day. They doubled
roughly every 25 hours. Monthly inflation hit an estimated 79.6 billion percent. The
three rounds. Then, in April 2009, it gave up. People switched to US dollars and rant.
In 2015, the old money was finally swapped. One US dollar for 35 quadrillion Zimbabwe
dollars. Your hundred trillion note? About 40 cents. Here's the twist. Collectors now
pay around $100 for one. That's the mirage. A number on paper isn't wealth. Money is
only worth what people trust. This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
